blocks.html_en: Overall, I am deeply concerned that we are moving way too fast, and I don’t think that is an unreasonable position given the facts outlined below.

sentences.en: Overall, I am deeply concerned that we are moving way too fast, and I don’t think that is an unreasonable position given the facts outlined below.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，我对我们的进展太快深感担忧，考虑到下面概述的事实，我认为这并不是一个不合理的立场。

blocks.html_en: AI as a phenomenon is capable of truly remarkable things, and scientists won a Nobel Prize for creating a very useful one. Whether large language models are actually beneficial for organizations as a whole is another matter. Using AI to produce larger documents more quickly, only for other departments to summarize them again with AI, is not progress. AI is also highly disruptive to organizational career structures: where will your future senior staff come from if AI takes over junior-level work? And will senior staff really enjoy spending their careers checking AI-generated output?

sentences.en: AI as a phenomenon is capable of truly remarkable things, and scientists won a Nobel Prize for creating a very useful one.
sentences.zh: 人工智能作为一种现象，能够做出真正非凡的事情，科学家们因创造了一种非常有用的人工智能而获得了诺贝尔奖。

sentences.en: Whether large language models are actually beneficial for organizations as a whole is another matter.
sentences.zh: 大型语言模型是否真的对整个组织有益是另一回事。

sentences.en: Using AI to produce larger documents more quickly, only for other departments to summarize them again with AI, is not progress.
sentences.zh: 利用AI更快地生成更大的文档，只是让其他部门用AI再次汇总，这并不是进步。

sentences.en: AI is also highly disruptive to organizational career structures: where will your future senior staff come from if AI takes over junior-level work?
sentences.zh: 人工智能对组织职业结构也具有高度颠覆性：如果人工智能接管初级工作，未来的高级员工将来自哪里？

sentences.en: And will senior staff really enjoy spending their careers checking AI-generated output?
sentences.zh: 高级员工真的会喜欢用他们的职业生涯来检查人工智能生成的输出吗？

blocks.html_en: Organizations are experiencing a strong Fear Of Missing Out that pushes them to adopt AI as quickly as possible. Yet despite how impressive AI really is, there is no urgency for most companies and institutions. If AI ultimately proves to be a good idea, it will still be there next year. Sometimes it seems as though people believe that if they don’t deploy now, they’ll never be able to catch up later.

sentences.en: Organizations are experiencing a strong Fear Of Missing Out that pushes them to adopt AI as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 组织正经历着强烈的“错失恐惧”，这促使他们尽快采用人工智能。

sentences.en: Yet despite how impressive AI really is, there is no urgency for most companies and institutions.
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管人工智能确实令人印象深刻，但大多数公司和机构都没有紧迫感。

sentences.en: If AI ultimately proves to be a good idea, it will still be there next year.
sentences.zh: 如果人工智能最终被证明是一个好主意，它明年仍然会存在。

sentences.en: Sometimes it seems as though people believe that if they don’t deploy now, they’ll never be able to catch up later.
sentences.zh: 有时，人们似乎相信，如果现在不部署，以后就永远无法赶上。

blocks.html_en: AI comes with enormous problems and risks that deserve careful consideration. It emits absurd amounts of CO2 and consumes so much electricity that additional power plants are being built just to support it, all while we’re already struggling with severe grid congestion and increasingly destructive wildfires. The intellectual property status of the data that goes into AI systems is a massive issue, and it also creates uncertainty about who owns the AI’s output.

sentences.en: AI comes with enormous problems and risks that deserve careful consideration.
sentences.zh: 人工智能带来了巨大的问题和风险，值得认真考虑。

sentences.en: It emits absurd amounts of CO2 and consumes so much electricity that additional power plants are being built just to support it, all while we’re already struggling with severe grid congestion and increasingly destructive wildfires.
sentences.zh: 它排放大量的二氧化碳，消耗大量的电力，以至于我们正在建造更多的发电厂来支持它，而与此同时，我们已经在与严重的电网拥堵和日益严重的野火作斗争。

sentences.en: The intellectual property status of the data that goes into AI systems is a massive issue, and it also creates uncertainty about who owns the AI’s output.
sentences.zh: 进入人工智能系统的数据的知识产权状况是一个大问题，它也给谁拥有人工智能输出带来了不确定性。

blocks.html_en: People brush these concerns aside surprisingly easily, but make no mistake: the AI industry will make them our problem. Try asking Microsoft whether they’ll indemnify you against intellectual property claims arising from Copilot’s output (a fun question to ask). Meanwhile, AI is disastrous for digital sovereignty: it’s surveillance capitalism all over again, imported from the United States. AI providers leak personal data on a massive scale, sometimes even data belonging to their own employees.

sentences.en: People brush these concerns aside surprisingly easily, but make no mistake: the AI industry will make them our problem.
sentences.zh: 人们出乎意料地轻易地忽视了这些担忧，但请不要误会：人工智能行业将使它们成为我们的问题。

sentences.en: Try asking Microsoft whether they’ll indemnify you against intellectual property claims arising from Copilot’s output (a fun question to ask).
sentences.zh: 尝试询问 Microsoft 他们是否会赔偿您因 Copilot 输出而产生的知识产权索赔（这是一个有趣的问题）。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, AI is disastrous for digital sovereignty: it’s surveillance capitalism all over again, imported from the United States.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，人工智能对数字主权来说是灾难性的：它又是从美国进口的监视资本主义。

sentences.en: AI providers leak personal data on a massive scale, sometimes even data belonging to their own employees.
sentences.zh: 人工智能提供商大规模泄露个人数据，有时甚至是属于自己员工的数据。

blocks.html_en: It’s difficult to know whom to listen to for advice. After investments totaling three or four trillion dollars, the AI industry itself is now so deeply committed that it can no longer be considered an impartial source. Much of the media, many consultants, and the broader software ecosystem have become so enthusiastic that it’s increasingly difficult to distinguish fact from hype. On the other hand, plenty of people feel so threatened by AI that they can only produce bad news about it. Then there are the moderates, who say, “AI is just a tool; it all depends on how you use it.” That’s true enough, but they never explain how to use it well, or if this is likely to happen, which makes the advice of limited practical value.

sentences.en: It’s difficult to know whom to listen to for advice.
sentences.zh: 很难知道该听谁的建议。

sentences.en: After investments totaling three or four trillion dollars, the AI industry itself is now so deeply committed that it can no longer be considered an impartial source.
sentences.zh: 在投资总额达到三四万亿美元之后，人工智能行业本身已经如此深入，以至于不能再被认为是公正的来源。

sentences.en: Much of the media, many consultants, and the broader software ecosystem have become so enthusiastic that it’s increasingly difficult to distinguish fact from hype.
sentences.zh: 许多媒体、许多顾问以及更广泛的软件生态系统都变得如此热情，以至于越来越难以区分事实和炒作。

sentences.en: On the other hand, plenty of people feel so threatened by AI that they can only produce bad news about it.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，很多人感到人工智能的威胁如此之大，以至于他们只能发布有关它的坏消息。

sentences.en: Then there are the moderates, who say, “AI is just a tool; it all depends on how you use it.”
sentences.zh: 然后是温和派，他们说，“人工智能只是一种工具；这完全取决于你如何使用它。”

sentences.en: That’s true enough, but they never explain how to use it well, or if this is likely to happen, which makes the advice of limited practical value.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，但他们从未解释如何很好地使用它，或者是否可能发生这种情况，这使得建议的实用价值有限。

blocks.html_en: The pressure to roll out AI is so great that most organizations never define their expectations in advance or establish how they’ll measure whether an AI experiment is successful. As a result, they end up with many vaguely defined “successes” that may not actually be successes at all. From the executive suite, everything quickly looks impressive. But are your employees actually becoming more productive or happier? Nobody measures this.

sentences.en: The pressure to roll out AI is so great that most organizations never define their expectations in advance or establish how they’ll measure whether an AI experiment is successful.
sentences.zh: 推出人工智能的压力如此之大，以至于大多数组织从未提前定义他们的期望或确定如何衡量人工智能实验是否成功。

sentences.en: As a result, they end up with many vaguely defined “successes” that may not actually be successes at all.
sentences.zh: 结果，他们最终获得了许多定义模糊的“成功”，而实际上可能根本不是成功。

sentences.zh: 从行政套房来看，一切很快就显得令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: But are your employees actually becoming more productive or happier?

blocks.html_en: There’s also the fundamental question of what we actually want from AI. It may seem appealing that AI makes writing reports and documents easier, but wasn’t writing those documents itself part of the thinking process that led to good plans? “Writing is thinking.” If you let AI do your writing, who actually learns anything from the exercise? Not you.

sentences.zh: 还有一个基本问题是我们到底想从人工智能中得到什么。

blocks.html_en: The companies providing AI services have also become financially precarious. There is considerable debate about whether the AI bubble is about to burst, or whether it is already beginning to do so. AI itself isn’t going away, but if today’s funding dries up, it could suddenly become much more expensive. That becomes a serious problem if your organization has, perhaps through staff turnover as well, become dependent on it.

sentences.zh: 提供人工智能服务的公司的财务状况也变得不稳定。

sentences.zh: 人工智能本身不会消失，但如果今天的资金枯竭，它可能会突然变得更加昂贵。

sentences.en: That becomes a serious problem if your organization has, perhaps through staff turnover as well, become dependent on it.
sentences.zh: 如果您的组织（也许还通过员工流动）变得依赖它，那么这将成为一个严重的问题。

blocks.html_en: In summary, the future of AI remains uncertain in many different ways. Its enormous potential (Nobel Prize!) is obvious, but that doesn’t mean everyone in an office should rush to have AI produce and read all of their documents. For most organizations, there is no train they’re in danger of missing.

blocks.html_en: A hasty decision to embrace AI, however, can cause enormous damage, to the climate, to your legal position, and to society through increased strain on the electricity grid. It can also drive away part of your workforce and leave you with an unsustainable organizational structure, because where will the next generation of senior staff come from?

blocks.html_en: In short: wise people don’t jump into the ditch just because everyone else is doing it. Take some time, wait and see, and you may spare your organization a great deal of disruption and unnecessary turmoil. A year from now, the picture will probably be much clearer.

sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，即使是不使用 Vivi 代码的开发人员也经常忽视提出这些问题。

blocks.html_en: The takeaway is that people, and especially executives, with personal positive AI experiences are not necessarily well positioned to decide on behalf of their organization whether AI has been a success. No matter how good it feels on a personal level. The same applies to people who use ChatGPT individually for work: it may feel great to have AI write and summarize reports for you, but is the organization actually becoming better as a result? That may not be your concern personally, but it certainly is the concern of management. I’ll return to that later.

sentences.en: The takeaway is that people, and especially executives, with personal positive AI experiences are not necessarily well positioned to decide on behalf of their organization whether AI has been a success.
sentences.zh: 得出的结论是，具有个人积极人工智能经验的人，尤其是高管，不一定能够代表其组织决定人工智能是否成功。

sentences.en: No matter how good it feels on a personal level.
sentences.zh: 无论个人感觉有多好。

sentences.en: The same applies to people who use ChatGPT individually for work: it may feel great to have AI write and summarize reports for you, but is the organization actually becoming better as a result?
sentences.zh: 这同样适用于单独使用 ChatGPT 进行工作的人：让人工智能为你编写和总结报告可能感觉很棒，但组织实际上是否因此而变得更好？

sentences.en: That may not be your concern personally, but it certainly is the concern of management.
sentences.zh: 这可能不是你个人关心的问题，但肯定是管理层关心的问题。

sentences.en: I’ll return to that later.
sentences.zh: 我稍后会回到这个话题。

blocks.html_en: An enormous problem is that in most organizations, people no longer evaluate whether AI is actually successful, or even can be. After all, it’s “the future.” AI is indeed here to stay, but it would still be nice to think carefully about what we should actually do with it. Or at the very least, define beforehand what you expect it to achieve and measure whether it actually does. Because “it felt good” simply isn’t enough. More on that later.

sentences.en: An enormous problem is that in most organizations, people no longer evaluate whether AI is actually successful, or even can be.
sentences.zh: 一个巨大的问题是，在大多数组织中，人们不再评估人工智能是否真正成功，甚至可以成功。

sentences.en: After all, it’s “the future.”
sentences.zh: 毕竟，这是“未来”。

sentences.en: AI is indeed here to stay, but it would still be nice to think carefully about what we should actually do with it.
sentences.zh: 人工智能确实会继续存在，但仔细思考我们实际上应该用它做什么仍然是件好事。

sentences.en: Or at the very least, define beforehand what you expect it to achieve and measure whether it actually does.
sentences.zh: 或者至少，预先定义您期望它实现的目标并衡量它是否确实实现了。

sentences.en: Because “it felt good” simply isn’t enough.
sentences.zh: 因为“感觉很好”还不够。

sentences.en: More on that later.
sentences.zh: 稍后会详细介绍。

blocks.html_en: Nevertheless, AI Isn’t Going Away

sentences.en: Nevertheless, AI Isn’t Going Away
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，人工智能并没有消失

blocks.html_en: History is full of new technologies that people initially had no idea what to do with. Today the laser is indispensable, yet for decades it was famously described as “a solution looking for a problem.”

sentences.en: History is full of new technologies that people initially had no idea what to do with.
sentences.zh: 历史上充满了人们最初不知道如何使用的新技术。

sentences.en: Today the laser is indispensable, yet for decades it was famously described as “a solution looking for a problem.”
sentences.zh: 今天，激光是不可或缺的，但几十年来，它一直被描述为“寻找问题的解决方案”。

blocks.html_en: People also laughed at the Internet. As if anyone would ever buy shoes or pizza online “yeah, right.” But look where we are now.

sentences.en: People also laughed at the Internet.
sentences.zh: 人们也在网上嘲笑。

sentences.en: As if anyone would ever buy shoes or pizza online “yeah, right.”
sentences.zh: 就好像有人会在网上购买鞋子或披萨一样“是的，没错。”

sentences.en: But look where we are now.
sentences.zh: 但看看我们现在在哪里。

blocks.html_en: But not everything becomes a success. We hardly hear about blockchain anymore, despite all the promises that it would solve every problem. Second Life, the Metaverse, and VR headsets also failed to live up to the hype.

sentences.en: But not everything becomes a success.
sentences.zh: 但并非一切都会成功。

sentences.en: We hardly hear about blockchain anymore, despite all the promises that it would solve every problem.
sentences.zh: 我们几乎不再听说区块链了，尽管人们都承诺它会解决所有问题。

sentences.en: Second Life, the Metaverse, and VR headsets also failed to live up to the hype.
sentences.zh: 《第二人生》、《元宇宙》和 VR 耳机也未能达到宣传的效果。

blocks.html_en: AI, however, seems much more likely to resemble the laser than a cryptocurrency. That Nobel Prize also was no joke. And you really can chat with AI and ask it to write or edit documents for you. Whether that ultimately turns out to be AI’s most valuable application remains to be seen, though.

sentences.en: AI, however, seems much more likely to resemble the laser than a cryptocurrency.
sentences.zh: 然而，人工智能似乎更像激光而不是加密货币。

sentences.en: That Nobel Prize also was no joke.
sentences.zh: 诺贝尔奖也不是开玩笑。

sentences.en: And you really can chat with AI and ask it to write or edit documents for you.
sentences.zh: 你真的可以与人工智能聊天并要求它为你编写或编辑文档。

sentences.en: Whether that ultimately turns out to be AI’s most valuable application remains to be seen, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这是否最终成为人工智能最有价值的应用还有待观察。

blocks.html_en: Having AI generate lengthy reports that are then read by other people using AI strikes me as a classic “horseless carriage.” The first motorized vehicles looked more like horse-drawn carriages without the horse than like modern automobiles. It took time for people to let go of old ways of thinking. I suspect the same is true of AI: right now we’re mostly using it to preserve existing practices (“documents that nobody reads anyway”).

sentences.en: Having AI generate lengthy reports that are then read by other people using AI strikes me as a classic “horseless carriage.”
sentences.zh: 让人工智能生成冗长的报告，然后由使用人工智能的其他人阅读，这让我觉得这是典型的“无马马车”。

sentences.en: The first motorized vehicles looked more like horse-drawn carriages without the horse than like modern automobiles.
sentences.zh: 第一辆机动车辆看起来更像是没有马的马车，而不是现代汽车。

sentences.en: It took time for people to let go of old ways of thinking.
sentences.zh: 人们需要时间才能放弃旧的思维方式。

sentences.en: I suspect the same is true of AI: right now we’re mostly using it to preserve existing practices (“documents that nobody reads anyway”).
sentences.zh: 我怀疑人工智能也是如此：现在我们主要使用它来保留现有的实践（“无论如何没人阅读的文档”）。

blocks.html_en: My guess is that we genuinely have no idea what we’ll be doing with AI ten years from now. But it certainly won’t be nothing. And it almost certainly won’t be “horse-drawn carriage without the horse.”

sentences.en: My guess is that we genuinely have no idea what we’ll be doing with AI ten years from now.
sentences.zh: 我的猜测是，我们真的不知道十年后我们会用人工智能做什么。

sentences.en: But it certainly won’t be nothing.
sentences.zh: 但肯定不会是什么都没有。

sentences.en: And it almost certainly won’t be “horse-drawn carriage without the horse.”
sentences.zh: 而且几乎可以肯定，它不会是“没有马的马车”。

blocks.html_en: Incidentally, even if the AI bubble bursts, AI itself won’t simply disappear. What will happen though is that it suddenly becomes much more expensive, temporarily relieving some of the pressure to use it. In fact, that increase in cost has already begun.

sentences.en: Incidentally, even if the AI bubble bursts, AI itself won’t simply disappear.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，即使人工智能泡沫破裂，人工智能本身也不会消失。

sentences.en: What will happen though is that it suddenly becomes much more expensive, temporarily relieving some of the pressure to use it.
sentences.zh: 但会发生的情况是，它突然变得更加昂贵，暂时缓解了一些使用它的压力。

sentences.en: In fact, that increase in cost has already begun.
sentences.zh: 事实上，成本的增加已经开始。

blocks.html_en: Who Should We Listen To?

sentences.en: Who Should We Listen To?
sentences.zh: 我们应该听谁的？

blocks.html_en: That’s not an easy question either. AI investments now amount to trillions of dollars. Entire industries, including the media, have been swept up in this tidal wave of money. For many consultancies and vendors, the success of AI has become existentially important.

sentences.en: That’s not an easy question either.
sentences.zh: 这也不是一个简单的问题。

sentences.en: AI investments now amount to trillions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 目前人工智能投资已达数万亿美元。

sentences.en: Entire industries, including the media, have been swept up in this tidal wave of money.
sentences.zh: 包括媒体在内的整个行业都被卷入了这股资金浪潮中。

sentences.en: For many consultancies and vendors, the success of AI has become existentially important.
sentences.zh: 对于许多咨询公司和供应商来说，人工智能的成功已经变得至关重要。

blocks.html_en: They’re overflowing with enthusiasm, but then, they have to be. The financial interests involved have become so enormous that the AI industry itself can no longer serve as an objective source of information. It’s like listening to a nearly bankrupt used-car dealer enthusiastically pitching you their last remaining car. Of course they’re enthusiastic. And unless something very unexpected happens, many AI companies are going to go bankrupt. So the analogy is rather fitting.

sentences.en: They’re overflowing with enthusiasm, but then, they have to be.
sentences.zh: 他们充满热情，但他们也必须如此。

sentences.en: The financial interests involved have become so enormous that the AI industry itself can no longer serve as an objective source of information.
sentences.zh: 所涉及的经济利益已经变得如此巨大，以至于人工智能行业本身已经不再能够作为客观的信息来源。

sentences.en: It’s like listening to a nearly bankrupt used-car dealer enthusiastically pitching you their last remaining car.
sentences.zh: 这就像听一个濒临破产的二手车经销商热情地向你推销他们最后一辆剩余的汽车。

sentences.en: Of course they’re enthusiastic.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们很热情。

sentences.en: And unless something very unexpected happens, many AI companies are going to go bankrupt.
sentences.zh: 除非发生非常意外的事情，否则许多人工智能公司将会破产。

sentences.en: So the analogy is rather fitting.
sentences.zh: 所以这个比喻还是比较恰当的。

blocks.html_en: Much of the media and many public commentators have also embraced the narrative that AI is simply inevitable. Entire “news sites” are now filled with AI-generated slop, so at the very least their shareholders clearly believe in it.

sentences.en: Much of the media and many public commentators have also embraced the narrative that AI is simply inevitable.
sentences.zh: 许多媒体和许多公共评论员也接受了人工智能是不可避免的这一说法。

sentences.en: Entire “news sites” are now filled with AI-generated slop, so at the very least their shareholders clearly believe in it.
sentences.zh: 整个“新闻网站”现在都充斥着人工智能生成的废话，因此至少他们的股东显然相信这一点。

blocks.html_en: A Dutch government ministry recently gave a presentation stating that, for civil servants, “using AI is now mandatory” (provided it’s done thoughtfully). Mandatory, apparently! The Dutch governing coalition has likewise embraced AI wholeheartedly and without reservation, as we also saw in the coalition agreement.

sentences.en: A Dutch government ministry recently gave a presentation stating that, for civil servants, “using AI is now mandatory” (provided it’s done thoughtfully).
sentences.zh: 荷兰政府部门最近在一次演讲中表示，对于公务员来说，“使用人工智能现在是强制性的”（前提是做得深思熟虑）。

sentences.en: Mandatory, apparently!
sentences.zh: 显然是强制性的！

sentences.en: The Dutch governing coalition has likewise embraced AI wholeheartedly and without reservation, as we also saw in the coalition agreement.
sentences.zh: 荷兰执政联盟同样全心全意、毫无保留地拥抱人工智能，正如我们在联盟协议中看到的那样。

blocks.html_en: Then there are, of course, the people who always seek nuance. They tend to offer compromises that aren’t particularly useful: AI is just a tool, and everything depends on how you use it. That’s true enough, for almost everything. But will people use it wisely? Do they know how? Are we teaching them? The moderates rarely discuss those questions. They also tend to argue that AI could work well under proper regulation, without mentioning that governments currently appear almost powerless in this area, and often don’t even seem interested in creating robust regulation, let alone enforcing it.

sentences.en: Then there are, of course, the people who always seek nuance.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有一些人总是追求细微差别。

sentences.en: They tend to offer compromises that aren’t particularly useful: AI is just a tool, and everything depends on how you use it.
sentences.zh: 他们倾向于提供并不是特别有用的妥协：人工智能只是一种工具，一切都取决于你如何使用它。

sentences.en: That’s true enough, for almost everything.
sentences.zh: 对于几乎所有事情来说，这都是事实。

sentences.en: But will people use it wisely?
sentences.zh: 但人们会明智地使用它吗？

sentences.en: Do they know how?
sentences.zh: 他们知道怎么做吗？

sentences.en: Are we teaching them?
sentences.zh: 我们在教他们吗？

sentences.en: The moderates rarely discuss those questions.
sentences.zh: 温和派很少讨论这些问题。

sentences.en: They also tend to argue that AI could work well under proper regulation, without mentioning that governments currently appear almost powerless in this area, and often don’t even seem interested in creating robust regulation, let alone enforcing it.
sentences.zh: 他们还倾向于认为，人工智能在适当的监管下可以很好地发挥作用，却没有提到政府目前在这一领域似乎几乎无能为力，而且往往似乎对制定强有力的监管不感兴趣，更不用说执行监管了。

blocks.html_en: Something else we shouldn’t overlook is how today’s use of LLMs, for text, images, video, and source code, comes across to people who take genuine pride and pleasure in creating those things with their own minds. It’s not just that many of us think we can do it better than the AI. It’s also intensely irritating to have people constantly confront us with their latest LLM creations and expect us to respond. The subtext is obvious: “I can now do, with my buddy Claude, what used to be your job.” Your days are numbered! Perhaps they don’t mean it that way, but that’s certainly how it comes across.

sentences.en: Something else we shouldn’t overlook is how today’s use of LLMs, for text, images, video, and source code, comes across to people who take genuine pride and pleasure in creating those things with their own minds.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该忽视的另一件事是，今天的法学硕士在文本、图像、视频和源代码方面的使用，给那些对用自己的想法创造这些东西感到真正自豪和高兴的人产生了怎样的影响。

sentences.en: It’s not just that many of us think we can do it better than the AI.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是我们很多人认为我们可以比人工智能做得更好。

sentences.en: It’s also intensely irritating to have people constantly confront us with their latest LLM creations and expect us to respond.
sentences.zh: 人们不断地向我们展示他们最新的法学硕士作品并期望我们做出回应，这也是非常令人恼火的。

sentences.en: The subtext is obvious: “I can now do, with my buddy Claude, what used to be your job.”
sentences.zh: 潜台词很明显：“我现在可以和我的好友克劳德一起做以前你的工作了。”

sentences.en: Your days are numbered!
sentences.zh: 你的日子屈指可数了！

sentences.en: Perhaps they don’t mean it that way, but that’s certainly how it comes across.
sentences.zh: 也许他们不是这个意思，但确实是这样。

blocks.html_en: It doesn’t help that we’re constantly told we have to get on board or risk being left behind. People who’ve never shipped an application in their lives tell me that my career as a software developer is over. The fact that software I wrote still powers half the Dutch Internet is dismissed as ancient history. I’m portrayed as some kind of tragic fossil who simply can’t keep up anymore.

sentences.en: It doesn’t help that we’re constantly told we have to get on board or risk being left behind.
sentences.zh: 我们不断被告知必须加入，否则就有被抛在后面的风险，这无济于事。

sentences.en: People who’ve never shipped an application in their lives tell me that my career as a software developer is over.
sentences.zh: 那些一生中从未发布过应用程序的人告诉我，我作为软件开发人员的职业生涯已经结束了。

sentences.en: The fact that software I wrote still powers half the Dutch Internet is dismissed as ancient history.
sentences.zh: 我编写的软件仍然为荷兰互联网的一半提供动力，这一事实已被视为古老的历史而被忽视。

sentences.en: I’m portrayed as some kind of tragic fossil who simply can’t keep up anymore.
sentences.zh: 我被描绘成某种悲剧性的化石，根本无法跟上。

blocks.html_en: When your life’s work is ridiculed like that, and your relevance is openly questioned, it’s extraordinarily difficult to maintain a balanced view of AI (though I do my best). And the entirely understandable resentment that results is then used by AI enthusiasts as an argument in itself: “You don’t have to listen to these bitter people.”

sentences.en: When your life’s work is ridiculed like that, and your relevance is openly questioned, it’s extraordinarily difficult to maintain a balanced view of AI (though I do my best).
sentences.zh: 当你一生的工作受到这样的嘲笑，并且你的相关性受到公开质疑时，要对人工智能保持平衡的看法就变得异常困难（尽管我尽力了）。

sentences.en: And the entirely understandable resentment that results is then used by AI enthusiasts as an argument in itself: “You don’t have to listen to these bitter people.”
sentences.zh: 由此产生的完全可以理解的怨恨情绪随后被人工智能爱好者用作论据：“你不必听这些痛苦的人的声音。”

blocks.html_en: Painfully enough, that’s partly true as well. People who are, quite understandably, deeply worried about AI often produce an endless stream of bad news about AI, whether that news is accurate or not.

sentences.en: Painfully enough, that’s partly true as well.
sentences.zh: 令人痛苦的是，这也部分正确。

sentences.en: People who are, quite understandably, deeply worried about AI often produce an endless stream of bad news about AI, whether that news is accurate or not.
sentences.zh: 可以理解的是，那些对人工智能深感担忧的人经常会发出源源不断的关于人工智能的坏消息，无论这些消息是否准确。

blocks.html_en: So if you want to form a well-founded opinion about AI today, you’re largely on your own. The industry, the media, the enthusiasts, and the critics all provide inconsistent signals that are difficult to make sense of. Even the nuanced folks can’t help you. Your own successful experiences with AI aren’t enough either, they cloud your judgment too much. And a personal dislike of AI doesn’t lead to balanced evaluations, either. In both directions, the same principle applies: feelings are not policy.

sentences.en: So if you want to form a well-founded opinion about AI today, you’re largely on your own.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你今天想对人工智能形成有根据的看法，你很大程度上只能靠自己。

sentences.en: The industry, the media, the enthusiasts, and the critics all provide inconsistent signals that are difficult to make sense of.
sentences.zh: 行业、媒体、爱好者和评论家都提供了难以理解的不一致信号。

sentences.en: Even the nuanced folks can’t help you.
sentences.zh: 即使是细致入微的人也无法帮助你。

sentences.en: Your own successful experiences with AI aren’t enough either, they cloud your judgment too much.
sentences.zh: 你自己在人工智能方面的成功经验也还不够，它们太多地影响了你的判断。

sentences.en: And a personal dislike of AI doesn’t lead to balanced evaluations, either.
sentences.zh: 个人对人工智能的厌恶也不会导致公正的评价。

sentences.en: In both directions, the same principle applies: feelings are not policy.
sentences.zh: 在这两个方向上，都适用同样的原则：感情不是政策。

blocks.html_en: The situation is well captured by this quotation, by the way:

sentences.en: The situation is well captured by this quotation, by the way:
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这句话很好地描述了这种情况：

blocks.html_en: “In his essay on Salvador Dali, Orwell argued that because Dali was a repulsive human being, the right wouldn’t admit that he was a great artist; conversely, because he was a great artist, the left wouldn’t admit he was a repulsive human being. I’m seeing the same thing with AI: because it’s unethical, one side won’t acknowledge that it’s useful, but because it’s useful, the other side won’t acknowledge that it’s unethical.” – Greg Wilson

blocks.html_en: AI Experiments in the Workplace and in Education

sentences.en: AI Experiments in the Workplace and in Education
sentences.zh: 工作场所和教育中的人工智能实验

blocks.html_en: The pressure is enormous, so everyone is rolling out AI in one form or another. Because apparently it simply has to happen, even when there’s no plan (read this piece!).

sentences.en: The pressure is enormous, so everyone is rolling out AI in one form or another.
sentences.zh: 压力是巨大的，所以每个人都在以这样或那样的形式推出人工智能。

sentences.en: Because apparently it simply has to happen, even when there’s no plan (read this piece!).
sentences.zh: 因为显然它必须发生，即使没有计划（阅读这篇文章！）。

blocks.html_en: If you’re running an AI experiment, make sure you actually measure whether it’s a success. To do that, you first need to define what you’re trying to achieve, and how you’ll measure whether you’ve achieved it.

sentences.en: If you’re running an AI experiment, make sure you actually measure whether it’s a success.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在进行人工智能实验，请确保你实际衡量它是否成功。

sentences.en: To do that, you first need to define what you’re trying to achieve, and how you’ll measure whether you’ve achieved it.
sentences.zh: 为此，您首先需要定义您想要实现的目标，以及如何衡量是否实现了目标。

blocks.html_en: The enthusiasm is so great that many AI experiments begin without any plan at all. The result is conclusions such as “the summaries look good,” or “24% of employees participated in the pilot.” Or sometimes not even that.

sentences.en: The enthusiasm is so great that many AI experiments begin without any plan at all.
sentences.zh: 人们的热情是如此之高，以至于许多人工智能实验在没有任何计划的情况下就开始了。

sentences.en: The result is conclusions such as “the summaries look good,” or “24% of employees participated in the pilot.”
sentences.zh: 结果是诸如“总结看起来不错”或“24% 的员工参与了试点”之类的结论。

sentences.en: Or sometimes not even that.
sentences.zh: 或者有时甚至不是这样。

blocks.html_en: Better metrics would be things like: “75% of the minister’s commitments were captured in the AI-generated summary,” or “25% of callers reported an error in the transcript of their conversation.”

sentences.en: Better metrics would be things like: “75% of the minister’s commitments were captured in the AI-generated summary,” or “25% of callers reported an error in the transcript of their conversation.”
sentences.zh: 更好的衡量标准是这样的：“75% 的部长承诺都包含在人工智能生成的摘要中”，或者“25% 的来电者报告了他们的谈话记录中的错误”。

blocks.html_en: Given the enormous expectations and pressure surrounding AI, proper evaluation is not something you can simply do as a hobby. There are specialists in workplace productivity and organizational effectiveness, and you should involve them before deciding, based purely on vibes, that your AI experiment is an astounding success.

sentences.en: Given the enormous expectations and pressure surrounding AI, proper evaluation is not something you can simply do as a hobby.
sentences.zh: 考虑到围绕人工智能的巨大期望和压力，正确的评估并不是简单地作为一种爱好就能做的事情。

sentences.en: There are specialists in workplace productivity and organizational effectiveness, and you should involve them before deciding, based purely on vibes, that your AI experiment is an astounding success.
sentences.zh: 在工作场所生产力和组织效率方面有专家，你应该让他们参与进来，然后再纯粹根据感觉决定你的人工智能实验取得了惊人的成功。

blocks.html_en: It’s remarkable how many AI pilots begin without anyone first deciding what the objective actually is. The pilot may then conclude with a “pointless cake celebration,” without anyone knowing what, if anything, has actually been achieved. It may even have made things worse.

sentences.en: It’s remarkable how many AI pilots begin without anyone first deciding what the objective actually is.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，有多少人工智能试点项目在没有人首先决定实际目标是什么的情况下就开始了。

sentences.en: The pilot may then conclude with a “pointless cake celebration,” without anyone knowing what, if anything, has actually been achieved.
sentences.zh: 然后，飞行员可能会以“毫无意义的蛋糕庆祝”结束，而没有人知道实际上已经取得了什么（如果有的话）。

sentences.en: It may even have made things worse.
sentences.zh: 它甚至可能让事情变得更糟。

blocks.html_en: As an example, here are the results of a study into Dutch municipal chatbots that are in production:

sentences.en: As an example, here are the results of a study into Dutch municipal chatbots that are in production:
sentences.zh: 例如，以下是对正在生产的荷兰市政聊天机器人的研究结果：

blocks.html_en: Source - 64% of questions were answered incorrectly, 10% correctly

sentences.en: Source - 64% of questions were answered incorrectly, 10% correctly
sentences.zh: 来源 - 64% 的问题回答错误，10% 回答正确

blocks.html_en: This result could easily have been avoided.

sentences.en: This result could easily have been avoided.
sentences.zh: 这个结果本来是可以轻易避免的。

blocks.html_en: Another problem is that management often announces an AI pilot with great enthusiasm, making it clear that they expect big things from it. Afterwards, employees are enthusiastic too. Because they saw senior management setting the example!

sentences.en: Another problem is that management often announces an AI pilot with great enthusiasm, making it clear that they expect big things from it.
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是，管理层经常以极大的热情宣布人工智能试点，明确表示他们对它抱有很大的期望。

sentences.en: Afterwards, employees are enthusiastic too.
sentences.zh: 随后，员工们也热情高涨。

sentences.en: Because they saw senior management setting the example!
sentences.zh: 因为他们看到高级管理层树立了榜样！

blocks.html_en: If you genuinely want to understand what’s happening on the work floor, which has always been difficult, by the way, you’ll need to conduct a credible anonymous survey. And you’ll also need to think about second-order effects.

sentences.en: If you genuinely want to understand what’s happening on the work floor, which has always been difficult, by the way, you’ll need to conduct a credible anonymous survey.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，如果你真的想了解工作场所正在发生的事情（这一直很困难），你需要进行一项可信的匿名调查。

sentences.en: And you’ll also need to think about second-order effects.
sentences.zh: 您还需要考虑二阶效应。

blocks.html_en: So don’t begin rolling out AI until you’ve defined what success looks like, what you expect from it, and how you’ll measure whether those expectations have been met. Otherwise, it’s all too easy for every experiment to become a “success.”

sentences.en: So don’t begin rolling out AI until you’ve defined what success looks like, what you expect from it, and how you’ll measure whether those expectations have been met.
sentences.zh: 因此，在定义成功是什么样子、您对成功的期望以及如何衡量这些期望是否得到满足之前，不要开始推出人工智能。

sentences.en: Otherwise, it’s all too easy for every experiment to become a “success.”
sentences.zh: 否则，每次实验都太容易“成功”。

blocks.html_en: What Do We Actually Want?

sentences.en: What Do We Actually Want?
sentences.zh: 我们真正想要什么？

blocks.html_en: Apparently, AI! And as quickly as possible too!

sentences.en: Apparently, AI!
sentences.zh: 显然，人工智能！

sentences.en: And as quickly as possible too!
sentences.zh: 而且也要尽快！

blocks.html_en: Still, it’s worth pausing to ask what an organization is actually trying to accomplish. A chatbot is not an objective in itself. Helping citizens or customers more quickly, more cheaply, and better, while remaining accurate, is an actual worthwhile objective.

sentences.en: Still, it’s worth pausing to ask what an organization is actually trying to accomplish.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，还是值得停下来问问一个组织实际上想要实现什么目标。

sentences.en: A chatbot is not an objective in itself.
sentences.zh: 聊天机器人本身并不是一个目标。

sentences.en: Helping citizens or customers more quickly, more cheaply, and better, while remaining accurate, is an actual worthwhile objective.
sentences.zh: 更快、更便宜、更好地帮助公民或客户，同时保持准确，是一个真正有价值的目标。

blocks.html_en: It’s certainly possible to use AI to produce enormous reports and documents at record speed. Then other people in the organization can use AI to summarize that stream of documents so they can understand it. That is not progress, even if no information were lost or hallucinated in the process, which, in reality, it often is.

sentences.en: It’s certainly possible to use AI to produce enormous reports and documents at record speed.
sentences.zh: 使用人工智能以创纪录的速度生成大量报告和文档当然是可能的。

sentences.en: Then other people in the organization can use AI to summarize that stream of documents so they can understand it.
sentences.zh: 然后组织中的其他人可以使用人工智能来总结该文档流，以便他们能够理解它。

sentences.en: That is not progress, even if no information were lost or hallucinated in the process, which, in reality, it often is.
sentences.zh: 即使在此过程中没有丢失任何信息或产生幻觉，这也不是进步，而事实上，情况往往如此。

blocks.html_en: People have long observed that writing and productive thinking are intimately connected. “Writing has been called the process by which you find out you don’t know what you are talking about.” Likewise, “Writing is thinking.” Another favorite: “If you’re thinking without writing, you only think you’re thinking.”

sentences.en: People have long observed that writing and productive thinking are intimately connected.
sentences.zh: 人们长期以来观察到写作和富有成效的思维密切相关。

sentences.en: “Writing has been called the process by which you find out you don’t know what you are talking about.”
sentences.zh: “写作被称为你发现自己不知道自己在说什么的过程。”

sentences.en: Likewise, “Writing is thinking.”
sentences.zh: 同样，“写作就是思考”。

sentences.en: Another favorite: “If you’re thinking without writing, you only think you’re thinking.”
sentences.zh: 另一条最喜欢的：“如果你在思考而不写作，你只是认为你在思考。”

blocks.html_en: Many internal documents ultimately aren’t read a lot or very well. But they are presented, discussed, and sometimes implemented. Until now, writing those documents has been an integral part of an organization’s thinking process. Formulating them made both the presentations and the plans themselves better. Even if a document wasn’t widely read, the fact that someone had written a substantial piece about an idea was a strong indication that they had genuinely invested time and thought into it.

sentences.en: Many internal documents ultimately aren’t read a lot or very well.
sentences.zh: 许多内部文件最终没有被读得很多或读得很好。

sentences.en: But they are presented, discussed, and sometimes implemented.
sentences.zh: 但它们被提出、讨论，有时甚至被实施。

sentences.en: Until now, writing those documents has been an integral part of an organization’s thinking process.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，编写这些文档一直是组织思维过程中不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: Formulating them made both the presentations and the plans themselves better.
sentences.zh: 制定它们可以使演示和计划本身变得更好。

sentences.en: Even if a document wasn’t widely read, the fact that someone had written a substantial piece about an idea was a strong indication that they had genuinely invested time and thought into it.
sentences.zh: 即使一份文件没有被广泛阅读，有人写了一篇关于某个想法的实质性文章这一事实就强烈表明他们确实投入了时间和思考。

blocks.html_en: With AI, however, it’s possible to produce superficially convincing documents with very little effort or reflection. Such a document is no longer evidence that someone has thought things through or put in significant work. And perhaps the results aren’t actually that good, either.

sentences.en: With AI, however, it’s possible to produce superficially convincing documents with very little effort or reflection.
sentences.zh: 然而，有了人工智能，只需很少的努力或反思就可以生成表面上令人信服的文档。

sentences.en: Such a document is no longer evidence that someone has thought things through or put in significant work.
sentences.zh: 这样的文件不再是某人已经深思熟虑或投入重要工作的证据。

sentences.en: And perhaps the results aren’t actually that good, either.
sentences.zh: 也许结果实际上也没有那么好。

blocks.html_en: My impression is that many organizations are unlikely to improve themselves if less genuine thinking takes place, or if the informal “did someone actually put real effort into this?” test no longer works.

sentences.en: My impression is that many organizations are unlikely to improve themselves if less genuine thinking takes place, or if the informal “did someone actually put real effort into this?”
sentences.zh: 我的印象是，如果不那么真诚的思考，或者如果非正式的“有人真的为此付出了真正的努力吗？”，许多组织就不太可能改进自己。

sentences.en: test no longer works.
sentences.zh: 测试不再有效。

blocks.html_en: That’s before we even consider the damage done when a public policy document turns out to be full of hallucinated references that don’t actually exist, something that even consultancies writing about AI keep doing in their own AI reports (additional link). Because we must definitely also not forget that even the best AI frequently generates absolute nonsense.

sentences.en: That’s before we even consider the damage done when a public policy document turns out to be full of hallucinated references that don’t actually exist, something that even consultancies writing about AI keep doing in their own AI reports (additional link).
sentences.zh: 那是在我们考虑当公共政策文件充满了实际上并不存在的幻觉引用时所造成的损害之前，甚至连撰写有关人工智能的咨询公司也在他们自己的人工智能报告中不断做的事情（附加链接）。

sentences.en: Because we must definitely also not forget that even the best AI frequently generates absolute nonsense.
sentences.zh: 因为我们绝对不能忘记，即使是最好的人工智能也经常会产生绝对的废话。

blocks.html_en: It’s therefore worth thinking very carefully about what you actually want AI to achieve before you begin deploying it.

sentences.en: It’s therefore worth thinking very carefully about what you actually want AI to achieve before you begin deploying it.
sentences.zh: 因此，在开始部署人工智能之前，值得仔细考虑您真正希望人工智能实现什么目标。

blocks.html_en: I recently attended a presentation by people who were using AI to read millions of newly written contracts so that the transactions described in them could be entered into a database. That’s a rather strange use of AI in 2026. Why aren’t those transactions simply entered into the database digitally in the first place, instead of being inferred from contracts written by humans? Or perhaps even contracts that were themselves drafted by AI. It could all have been done directly.

sentences.en: I recently attended a presentation by people who were using AI to read millions of newly written contracts so that the transactions described in them could be entered into a database.
sentences.zh: 我最近参加了一个演讲，人们使用人工智能读取数百万份新写的合同，以便将其中描述的交易输入数据库。

sentences.en: That’s a rather strange use of AI in 2026.
sentences.zh: 在 2026 年，人工智能的应用相当奇怪。

sentences.en: Why aren’t those transactions simply entered into the database digitally in the first place, instead of being inferred from contracts written by humans?
sentences.zh: 为什么这些交易不首先以数字方式简单地输入数据库，而不是从人类编写的合同中推断出来？

sentences.en: Or perhaps even contracts that were themselves drafted by AI.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能是人工智能本身起草的合同。

sentences.en: It could all have been done directly.
sentences.zh: 这一切都可以直接完成。

blocks.html_en: At the same time, if you have millions of historical contracts whose contents aren’t in a database, it’s hardly “better” to have people read them manually and copy the data over. That’s not enjoyable work either. Verifying that the AI extracted everything correctly is difficult enough.

sentences.en: At the same time, if you have millions of historical contracts whose contents aren’t in a database, it’s hardly “better” to have people read them manually and copy the data over.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，如果您有数百万个历史合约，其内容不在数据库中，那么让人们手动读取它们并复制数据也很难“更好”。

sentences.en: That’s not enjoyable work either.
sentences.zh: 这也不是令人愉快的工作。

sentences.en: Verifying that the AI extracted everything correctly is difficult enough.
sentences.zh: 验证人工智能是否正确提取所有内容已经够困难的了。

blocks.html_en: Another nice example I heard involved a government agency that wanted to use AI to automate part of a process, but quickly discovered that the input data was far too messy for this to work. Once they cleaned up the data, the existing process improved so much that they no longer needed an AI version at all. Of course, that won’t always happen, but it’s worth remembering that AI isn’t magic: it requires good input. Many companies discover this when they try to build a chatbot that understands their business processes. If those processes aren’t documented properly anywhere, the chatbot won’t perform miracles to fix that. That’s when hallucinations become a real risk.

sentences.en: Another nice example I heard involved a government agency that wanted to use AI to automate part of a process, but quickly discovered that the input data was far too messy for this to work.
sentences.zh: 我听到的另一个很好的例子涉及一个政府机构，该机构希望使用人工智能来自动化部分流程，但很快发现输入数据太混乱，无法实现。

sentences.en: Once they cleaned up the data, the existing process improved so much that they no longer needed an AI version at all.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们清理了数据，现有流程就会得到很大改进，以至于他们根本不再需要人工智能版本。

sentences.en: Of course, that won’t always happen, but it’s worth remembering that AI isn’t magic: it requires good input.
sentences.zh: 当然，这种情况不会总是发生，但值得记住的是，人工智能并不神奇：它需要良好的输入。

sentences.en: Many companies discover this when they try to build a chatbot that understands their business processes.
sentences.zh: 许多公司在尝试构建理解其业务流程的聊天机器人时发现了这一点。

sentences.en: If those processes aren’t documented properly anywhere, the chatbot won’t perform miracles to fix that.
sentences.zh: 如果这些流程没有在任何地方正确记录，聊天机器人就不会奇迹般地解决这个问题。

sentences.en: That’s when hallucinations become a real risk.
sentences.zh: 那时幻觉就成为真正的风险。

blocks.html_en: Doing “AI for AI’s sake” is an expensive hobby, and a risky one. Plenty can go wrong. It’s perfectly reasonable to spend some time thinking about that first.

sentences.en: Doing “AI for AI’s sake” is an expensive hobby, and a risky one.
sentences.zh: “为了人工智能而人工智能”是一种昂贵且冒险的爱好。

sentences.en: Plenty can go wrong.
sentences.zh: 很多事情都可能出错。

sentences.en: It’s perfectly reasonable to spend some time thinking about that first.
sentences.zh: 首先花一些时间思考这一点是完全合理的。

blocks.html_en: What Is the Right Pace?

sentences.en: What Is the Right Pace?
sentences.zh: 什么是正确的步伐？

blocks.html_en: Right now, organizations are under enormous pressure to “get started with AI.” After all, who wouldn’t want to be seen as a modern organization?

sentences.en: Right now, organizations are under enormous pressure to “get started with AI.”
sentences.zh: 目前，组织面临着“开始使用人工智能”的巨大压力。

sentences.en: After all, who wouldn’t want to be seen as a modern organization?
sentences.zh: 毕竟，谁不想被视为现代组织呢？

blocks.html_en: Still, it’s worth taking a step back and evaluating all this urgency. First, the downsides of moving slowly:

sentences.en: Still, it’s worth taking a step back and evaluating all this urgency.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，还是值得退后一步并评估所有这些紧迫性。

sentences.en: First, the downsides of moving slowly:
sentences.zh: 首先，缓慢移动的缺点：

blocks.html_en: • You may miss out on potential cost savings.

sentences.en: You may miss out on potential cost savings.
sentences.zh: 您可能会错过潜在的成本节省。

blocks.html_en: • Some employees may simply expect AI to be available.

sentences.en: Some employees may simply expect AI to be available.
sentences.zh: 一些员工可能只是希望人工智能可用。

blocks.html_en: There is also a general fear of “missing the boat.” But many organizations (governments, for example) are not locked in a fierce battle with competitors. That boat will still be there next year. AI is not going to disappear overnight. And so far, organizations do not appear to be seeing measurable productivity gains from AI. That may well change, but for now you’re not missing much. Also, deploying office AI tools does not mean you are now “a future-proofed AI company”.

sentences.en: There is also a general fear of “missing the boat.”
sentences.zh: 人们还普遍担心“错失良机”。

sentences.en: But many organizations (governments, for example) are not locked in a fierce battle with competitors.
sentences.zh: 但许多组织（例如政府）并没有陷入与竞争对手的激烈战斗中。

sentences.en: That boat will still be there next year.
sentences.zh: 明年那艘船仍然在那里。

sentences.en: AI is not going to disappear overnight.
sentences.zh: 人工智能不会在一夜之间消失。

sentences.en: And so far, organizations do not appear to be seeing measurable productivity gains from AI.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，组织似乎还没有看到人工智能带来可衡量的生产力提升。

sentences.en: That may well change, but for now you’re not missing much.
sentences.zh: 这很可能会改变，但目前你并没有错过太多。

sentences.en: Also, deploying office AI tools does not mean you are now “a future-proofed AI company”.
sentences.zh: 此外，部署办公人工智能工具并不意味着你现在是“一家面向未来的人工智能公司”。

blocks.html_en: Point 2 is a more significant concern. Someone who has spent years creating and analyzing documents with AI may no longer be able to do that work manually. This surprised me too, but someone from a large HR department told me about the problem. A new class of employees has emerged that no longer functions effectively without AI assistance. Their own skills deteriorate rapidly through cognitive offloading.

sentences.en: Point 2 is a more significant concern.
sentences.zh: 第 2 点是更重要的问题。

sentences.en: Someone who has spent years creating and analyzing documents with AI may no longer be able to do that work manually.
sentences.zh: 花费数年时间使用人工智能创建和分析文档的人可能无法再手动完成这项工作。

sentences.en: This surprised me too, but someone from a large HR department told me about the problem.
sentences.zh: 这也让我感到惊讶，但是一个大型人力资源部门的人告诉了我这个问题。

sentences.en: A new class of employees has emerged that no longer functions effectively without AI assistance.
sentences.zh: 新一代员工已经出现，如果没有人工智能的帮助，他们将无法有效工作。

sentences.en: Their own skills deteriorate rapidly through cognitive offloading.
sentences.zh: 由于认知卸载，他们自己的技能迅速恶化。

blocks.html_en: Moving too quickly has downsides as well:

sentences.en: Moving too quickly has downsides as well:
sentences.zh: 行动太快也有缺点：

blocks.html_en: • Violating climate agreements, the questionable intellectual property situation, and broader ethical concerns.

sentences.en: Violating climate agreements, the questionable intellectual property situation, and broader ethical concerns.
sentences.zh: 违反气候协议、可疑的知识产权状况以及更广泛的道德问题。

blocks.html_en: • Employees may leave because of AI.

sentences.en: Employees may leave because of AI.
sentences.zh: 员工可能会因为人工智能而离开。

blocks.html_en: • Declining quality of service.

sentences.en: Declining quality of service.
sentences.zh: 服务质量下降。

blocks.html_en: • Violating the privacy and rights of citizens, customers, or other contacts.

sentences.en: Violating the privacy and rights of citizens, customers, or other contacts.
sentences.zh: 侵犯公民、客户或其他联系人的隐私和权利。

blocks.html_en: • Further erosion of digital sovereignty.

sentences.en: Further erosion of digital sovereignty.
sentences.zh: 数字主权进一步受到侵蚀。

blocks.html_en: • If the AI bubble bursts, everything may suddenly become unaffordable.

sentences.en: If the AI bubble bursts, everything may suddenly become unaffordable.
sentences.zh: 如果人工智能泡沫破灭，一切可能会突然变得难以承受。

blocks.html_en: • Reduced organizational thinking capacity.

sentences.en: Reduced organizational thinking capacity.
sentences.zh: 组织思维能力下降。

blocks.html_en: • Disruption of the career pipeline (“all the juniors are gone, where will future seniors come from?”)

sentences.en: Disruption of the career pipeline (“all the juniors are gone, where will future seniors come from?”)
sentences.zh: 职业管道的中断（“所有的后辈都走了，未来的前辈从哪里来？”）

content_html_zh:
最近，我连续向荷兰政府服务提供商网络和荷兰科学、技术和创新咨询委员会做了关于人工智能的两次演讲。 在这两个不同的简短演讲中，我希望分享一些对当前掌舵者、能够或必须做出人工智能政策决策的人有用的见解。 非常感谢 NPD 和 AWTI 的邀请和激动人心的讨论！

🇳🇱 这篇文章还有荷兰语版本。

本文源自这两个演示。 第一个是在 NPD，重点关注决策者面临的具体挑战。 第二个是在 AWTI 上，主题是构建值得信赖的（欧洲）人工智能基础设施所需的内容。 并且，就此而言，还触及了这实际上意味着什么。 在这些演示之后，我开始写作，并最终提出了这篇文章。

在写作时，我发现这个主题确实具有挑战性。 有人工智能的热情拥护者，也有人相信人工智能是魔鬼的化身。 这些阵营是如此两极分化，不可能写出让所有人都满意的东西。

然而，完全有可能写出一篇让每个人都对某些部分感到愤怒的文章。 所以就这样吧。

我确实希望支持者和反对者都能从这篇文章中变得更加明智。 或许有一件事我们都可以达成共识：到底什么是匆忙？ 今年每个城市真的需要部署 Copilot 吗？ 荷兰议会真的必须为所有人推出它吗？

接下来的内容并不是“双方”的争论。 对于那些完全不喜欢人工智能的人来说，你会在下面发现人工智能确实可以做一些了不起的事情。 对于人工智能爱好者来说，我有一长串的理由来仔细思考这是否真的是一个好主意。

总的来说，我对我们的进展太快深感担忧，考虑到下面概述的事实，我认为这并不是一个不合理的立场。

当你一生的工作受到这样的嘲笑，并且你的相关性受到公开质疑时，要对人工智能保持平衡的看法就变得异常困难（尽管我尽力了）。 由此产生的完全可以理解的怨恨情绪随后被人工智能爱好者用作论据：“你不必听这些痛苦的人的声音。”

令人痛苦的是，这也部分正确。 可以理解的是，那些对人工智能深感担忧的人经常会发出源源不断的关于人工智能的坏消息，无论这些消息是否准确。

因此，如果你今天想对人工智能形成有根据的看法，你很大程度上只能靠自己。 行业、媒体、爱好者和评论家都提供了难以理解的不一致信号。 即使是细致入微的人也无法帮助你。 你自己在人工智能方面的成功经验也还不够，它们太多地影响了你的判断。 个人对人工智能的厌恶也不会导致公正的评价。 在这两个方向上，都适用同样的原则：感情不是政策。

顺便说一句，这句话很好地描述了这种情况：

奥威尔在他关于萨尔瓦多·达利的文章中指出，因为达利是一个令人厌恶的人，右派不会承认他是一个伟大的艺术家；相反，因为他是一个伟大的艺术家，左派也不会承认他是一个令人厌恶的人。 我在人工智能上也看到了同样的情况：因为它不道德，一方不会承认它有用，但因为它有用，另一方也不会承认它不道德。” ——格雷格·威尔逊

工作场所和教育中的人工智能实验

压力是巨大的，所以每个人都在以这样或那样的形式推出人工智能。 因为显然它必须发生，即使没有计划（阅读这篇文章！）。

如果你正在进行人工智能实验，请确保你实际衡量它是否成功。 为此，您首先需要定义您想要实现的目标，以及如何衡量是否实现了目标。

人们的热情是如此之高，以至于许多人工智能实验在没有任何计划的情况下就开始了。 结果是诸如“总结看起来不错”或“24% 的员工参与了试点”之类的结论。 或者有时甚至不是这样。

更好的衡量标准是这样的：“75% 的部长承诺都包含在人工智能生成的摘要中”，或者“25% 的来电者报告了他们的谈话记录中的错误”。

考虑到围绕人工智能的巨大期望和压力，正确的评估并不是简单地作为一种爱好就能做的事情。 在工作场所生产力和组织效率方面有专家，你应该让他们参与进来，然后再纯粹根据感觉决定你的人工智能实验取得了惊人的成功。

值得注意的是，有多少人工智能试点项目在没有人首先决定实际目标是什么的情况下就开始了。 然后，飞行员可能会以“毫无意义的蛋糕庆祝”结束，而没有人知道实际上已经取得了什么（如果有的话）。 它甚至可能让事情变得更糟。

例如，以下是对正在生产的荷兰市政聊天机器人的研究结果：

来源 - 64% 的问题回答错误，10% 回答正确

这个结果本来是可以轻易避免的。

另一个问题是，管理层经常以极大的热情宣布人工智能试点，明确表示他们对它抱有很大的期望。 随后，员工们也热情高涨。 因为他们看到高级管理层树立了榜样！

顺便说一句，如果你真的想了解工作场所正在发生的事情（这一直很困难），你需要进行一项可信的匿名调查。 您还需要考虑二阶效应。

因此，在定义成功是什么样子、您对成功的期望以及如何衡量这些期望是否得到满足之前，不要开始推出人工智能。 否则，每次实验都太容易“成功”。

我们真正想要什么？

显然，人工智能！ 而且也要尽快！

尽管如此，还是值得停下来问问一个组织实际上想要实现什么目标。 聊天机器人本身并不是一个目标。 更快、更便宜、更好地帮助公民或客户，同时保持准确，是一个真正有价值的目标。

使用人工智能以创纪录的速度生成大量报告和文档当然是可能的。 然后组织中的其他人可以使用人工智能来总结该文档流，以便他们能够理解它。 即使在此过程中没有丢失任何信息或产生幻觉，这也不是进步，而事实上，情况往往如此。

人们长期以来观察到写作和富有成效的思维密切相关。 “写作被称为你发现自己不知道自己在说什么的过程。” 同样，“写作就是思考”。 另一条最喜欢的：“如果你在思考而不写作，你只是认为你在思考。”

许多内部文件最终没有被读得很多或读得很好。 但它们被提出、讨论，有时甚至被实施。 到目前为止，编写这些文档一直是组织思维过程中不可或缺的一部分。 制定它们可以使演示和计划本身变得更好。 即使一份文件没有被广泛阅读，有人写了一篇关于某个想法的实质性文章这一事实就强烈表明他们确实投入了时间和思考。

然而，有了人工智能，只需很少的努力或反思就可以生成表面上令人信服的文档。 这样的文件不再是某人已经深思熟虑或投入重要工作的证据。 也许结果实际上也没有那么好。

我的印象是，如果不那么真诚的思考，或者如果非正式的“有人真的为此付出了真正的努力吗？”，许多组织就不太可能改进自己。 测试不再有效。

那是在我们考虑当公共政策文件充满了实际上并不存在的幻觉引用时所造成的损害之前，甚至连撰写有关人工智能的咨询公司也在他们自己的人工智能报告中不断做的事情（附加链接）。 因为我们绝对不能忘记，即使是最好的人工智能也经常会产生绝对的废话。

因此，在开始部署人工智能之前，值得仔细考虑您真正希望人工智能实现什么目标。

我最近参加了一个演讲，人们使用人工智能读取数百万份新写的合同，以便将其中描述的交易输入数据库。 在 2026 年，人工智能的应用相当奇怪。 为什么这些交易不首先以数字方式简单地输入数据库，而不是从人类编写的合同中推断出来？ 甚至可能是人工智能本身起草的合同。 这一切都可以直接完成。

与此同时，如果您有数百万个历史合约，其内容不在数据库中，那么让人们手动读取它们并复制数据也很难“更好”。 这也不是令人愉快的工作。 验证人工智能是否正确提取所有内容已经够困难的了。

我听到的另一个很好的例子涉及一个政府机构，该机构希望使用人工智能来自动化部分流程，但很快发现输入数据太混乱，无法实现。 一旦他们清理了数据，现有流程就会得到很大改进，以至于他们根本不再需要人工智能版本。 当然，这种情况不会总是发生，但值得记住的是，人工智能并不神奇：它需要良好的输入。 许多公司在尝试构建理解其业务流程的聊天机器人时发现了这一点。 如果这些流程没有在任何地方正确记录，聊天机器人就不会奇迹般地解决这个问题。 那时幻觉就成为真正的风险。

“为了人工智能而人工智能”是一种昂贵且冒险的爱好。 很多事情都可能出错。 首先花一些时间思考这一点是完全合理的。

什么是正确的步伐？

目前，组织面临着“开始使用人工智能”的巨大压力。 毕竟，谁不想被视为现代组织呢？

尽管如此，还是值得退后一步并评估所有这些紧迫性。 首先，缓慢移动的缺点：

  1. 您可能会错过潜在的成本节省。
  2. 一些员工可能只是希望人工智能可用。

人们还普遍担心“错失良机”。 但许多组织（例如政府）并没有陷入与竞争对手的激烈战斗中。 明年那艘船仍然在那里。 人工智能不会在一夜之间消失。 到目前为止，组织似乎还没有看到人工智能带来可衡量的生产力提升。 这很可能会改变，但目前你并没有错过太多。 此外，部署办公人工智能工具并不意味着你现在是“一家面向未来的人工智能公司”。

第 2 点是更重要的问题。 花费数年时间使用人工智能创建和分析文档的人可能无法再手动完成这项工作。 这也让我感到惊讶，但是一个大型人力资源部门的人告诉了我这个问题。 新一代员工已经出现，如果没有人工智能的帮助，他们将无法有效工作。 由于认知卸载，他们自己的技能迅速恶化。

行动太快也有缺点：

  1. 违反气候协议、可疑的知识产权状况以及更广泛的道德问题。
  2. 员工可能会因为人工智能而离开。
  3. 服务质量下降。
  4. 侵犯公民、客户或其他联系人的隐私和权利。
  5. 数字主权进一步受到侵蚀。
  6. 如果人工智能泡沫破灭，一切可能会突然变得难以承受。
  7. 组织思维能力下降。
  8. 职业管道的中断（“所有的后辈都走了，未来的前辈从哪里来？”）

关于第一点：从高管层来看，事情往往看起来与在工作场所非常不同，在工作场所，员工听到他们的主管热情地宣布他们的工作很快将实现自动化。 这并不一定会有好结果。

关于第 2 点：请参阅上面的聊天机器人示例。 即使现在被认为是“现代的”，事情通常也不会改善。

关于第三点：人工智能实验已多次被证明会泄露大量个人数据。 例如，Meta（Facebook）最近在内部人工智能试验中泄露了敏感的员工数据。

至于您的客户、申请人和其他联系人的权利，人们很容易忘记我们在欧洲同时拥有《人工智能法案》和《通用数据保护条例》。 这些法律对如何使用人工智能筛选和拒绝求职者施加了具体规则。 在您不知不觉中，人力资源部门的某人正在以您从未批准的方式使用人工智能，但您的组织仍然违规。 尽管许多人声称，《人工智能法案》的主要条款确实在今年生效。

关于第四点：我们据称正在努力减少对欧洲美国科技公司的依赖。 然而，绝大多数工作场所人工智能来自大型科​​技公司，以及那些渴望收集、存储和重用尽可能多的数据以用于未来人工智能培训的公司。

我在上面讨论了组织思维能力的降低。 简单地写下计划本身就是一种更清晰思考的有效方法。 如果你让人工智能来写作，你就会失去这种宝贵的好处。

至于最后一点，我们将进入下一部分。

职业管道

如果让人工智能接管初级工作，我们就要问未来的高级员工从哪里来。 老实说，我不知道。 但如果您的组织依赖于结构化的职业阶梯，那么明智的做法是找到答案。 人才管道的损坏需要数年时间才能修复。

人工智能可以完成大部分工作，而人类只需监督它。 但这从根本上改变了人们的工作，事实证明，人类并不特别适合将大部分工作时间花在“检查计算机做了什么”。 你最终可能会赶走经验丰富的高级员工，他们对这样的角色没什么兴趣。 与此同时，初级人员不再被需要，因为人工智能已经取代了他们的工作。

这听起来可能很戏剧化，但事实上，这已经发生了。

当组织像荷兰内阁那样宣布他们“完全致力于人工智能”时，他们还需要考虑更广泛的后果。 几年后我们还会有一个健康、运转良好的组织吗？

“它总是有效的！”

每当你担心未来的高级员工将来自哪里时，人工智能爱好者几乎总是回答说这些事情总会自行解决。 新的工作将会出现，以前不存在的工作。 “市场会找到出路。”

他们经常援引工业革命，但却忽略了，事情“成功”之前经历了几代人的艰辛，同时条件也很糟糕。

其他人则未经证实地声称，他们现在有更多时间思考，因为人工智能可以处理写作。 还有一些人认为，人工智能今天可能不会产生真正的新想法，但将来肯定会产生，因此现在让人工智能思考已经可以接受。

这些都是很有吸引力的主张，但也需要相当大的信心才能接受。 请出示证据。

在围绕人工智能重塑组织之前仔细思考并没有什么不合理的，即使人们错误地提到工业革命作为一切最终都会好起来的证据。

那么，现在怎么办？

截至 2026 年 7 月，有一件事相当明确：围绕人工智能的炒作巨大，但其最终走向仍然高度不确定。 还有令人信服的法律、道德、环境和财务原因需要谨慎对待。 最重要的是，人工智能可能会对劳动力以及公民或客户的隐私产生严重且意想不到的后果。

像这样的批评常常被驳回，“好吧，那只是一个讨厌人工智能的人。” 但这太简单了。 我们正在谈论的可能是工作场所历史上最大的变革，而各组织正以惊人的速度投入其中。 还有很多令人担忧的客观原因（见上文）。 这些都值得仔细考虑，这意味着认真对待批评而不是忽视信息使者。

好消息是，对于大多数组织来说，并不存在真正的紧迫性。 如果您不在 2026 年推出 Copilot，您仍有机会在 2027 年推出。 到那时，今天的许多不确定因素将变得更加清晰。 主要诉讼可能已经取得进展，一些实力较弱的人工智能公司可能已经破产，价格可能会更高但也更现实，欧盟人工智能法案的实际影响将得到更好的理解，这可能会让您避免代价高昂的合规错误。

也许更重要的是，到那时我们将从首先冲入的组织中学到很多东西。 他们真的受益了吗？ 或者他们最终遇到了严重的问题？

与此同时，如果您的组织决定尝试人工智能，请不要犯今天许多其他人正在犯的同样错误。 预先定义您希望通过人工智能实验实现的目标，并准确指定如何衡量它是否成功。 “感觉很好”是从根本上改变组织运作方式的一个相当薄弱的理由。 如果你严格地评估你的实验，如果结果证明它们不值得，你就不太可能后悔。

再次强调，不要忘记围绕人工智能和人工智能公司本身以及其中许多公司的运营方式的基本问题。 当你采用人工智能时，你也选择与这些地方开展业务。 你至少能做的就是承认这个事实（就像我在翻译这篇文章时所做的那样）。

祝你好运。 人工智能不会消失，但这个故事的结局在很大程度上仍然取决于我们。
